Subject: May 4 cross-functional digest — outstanding decisions & next steps

Thanks team — quick recap from today’s cross-functional sync and the outstanding items we need closed before QBR prep on Friday. I tried to keep this short and assign clear owners.

Top outstanding asks (owner):
- Acme data access & sample dataset (Marissa) — Acme asked for an anonymized sample to validate latency/throughput assumptions. They also asked about retention policy.
- SLA exception for extra throughput during pilot (Lauren) — Acme requests a temporary throughput bump for first 30 days; they want a written exception.
- Runbook for fallback behavior (Vivek / Markus) — need a short rollback and failover runbook we can share with CS and Infra.
- QBR slide: economic impact of batching+quantization (Monica/Markus) — want one slide with expected cost delta and risk level.

Action items (due dates):
- Marissa: get sample dataset and contact at Acme (Due: 2027-05-03 EOD) — please request the sanitized CSV and confirm columns.
- Lauren: draft SLA exception wording and scope (Due: 2027-05-03 noon) — include duration, metrics, and hitless rollback conditions.
- Vivek: propose two fallback approaches (rolling fallback to smaller model; traffic split to dedicated pool) and effort estimate (Due: 2027-05-04 morning).
- Markus: produce a one-page runbook and cost slide input (Due: 2027-05-04 EOD).

Attachments: I’ve dropped the QBR staffing matrix and the suggested slide template in Drive (link below). If you need me to call Acme directly, I’m available after 2pm PT tomorrow.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QBRPrepsDoc

Thanks Monica — quick clarifications from product side:

- On the SLA exception: we can scope a 30-day pilot exception but need explicit throughput bounds and an agreed rollback trigger (e.g., 5% error-rate increase OR sustained token latency > 1.5x baseline). I’ll draft a short memo with the triggers.
- Acme’s retention question: legal prefers the default 30-day ephemeral cache with opt-in log retention for pilot customers. Marissa, can you confirm Acme’s compliance team will accept that?

Also: I think the cost slide should show two scenarios (with and without prefix caching) because their workload is heavy on repeated prompts. If they can provide a sample of 1,000 sessions we should run quick simulations.

—
Lauren Bishop

Quick technical take after a short spike this morning:

Options to satisfy pilot throughput with graceful fallback:
1) Traffic split to Dedicated pool (low dev effort, medium ops cost). Pros: predictable latency; Cons: extra infra cost, requires infra signoff. Estimated 2 business days to provision. Jira: INF-1284 created.
2) Rolling fallback to smaller quantized model when queue depth > threshold (higher engineering lift, lower recurring cost). Pros: cost saver; Cons: potential quality delta for edge prompts. Effort: ~1 week to ship safe gating.

Runbook items I’ll draft:
- How to detect degradation (95th pct token latency, error-rate thresholds)
- Migration steps for Dedicated pool split (traffic, warm caches)
- Quick rollback steps (DNS/route toggle or config flag)

I’ll drop a one-page runbook draft to the Drive link by EOD and open INF-1284 with steps and owners. Markus, I’ll need your input on the ops checklist for provisioning.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

- Fallback approach: proceed with traffic split to Dedicated pool as short-term mitigation (Owner: Vivek/Markus to provision; target: 2027-05-10)
- Customer-facing runbook: Vivek/Markus to deliver one-page runbook and a short FAQ for CS (Due: 2027-05-07)

QBR roles:
